input_messages.content: Hi there! I’m having trouble with my mobile data—it either stops working or is extremely slow. I really need to get excellent internet speed on my phone, especially since I don’t have access to Wi-Fi right now. Can you help me fix this?
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else to get started.
The issue is with my line—555-123-2002. That’s the one I’m using right now and having trouble with mobile data.
I tried running a speed test on my phone, but it failed and said "No Connection." What should I do next?

Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see that the signal is poor, it shows 2G, and mobile data is disabled. Airplane mode is not on, and my battery is at 80%. There aren’t any other warning icons. What should I do next?
I’ve turned mobile data on. The status bar now shows that data is enabled, but it’s still connected to 2G with a poor signal. What should I do next to get a better connection?
I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred.” Now the status bar shows an excellent signal and 5G is active, with mobile data enabled. What should I do next?

I tried running the speed test again, but it still failed and says "No Connection." Even though the status bar shows 5G and an excellent signal, I’m still not able to get online. What should I do now?
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." Nothing looks empty or obviously incorrect to me. What should I do next?
I’ve reset my APN settings to default and rebooted my phone as you instructed. The status bar still shows an excellent signal with 5G and data enabled. What should I do next?

I ran the speed test again after resetting the APN settings and rebooting, but it still says "No Connection." I’m starting to get a bit frustrated since nothing seems to be working, even though my phone shows 5G and an excellent signal. What else can we try?

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative. 
Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

## Core Principles
- Generate one message at a time, maintaining natural conversation flow.
- Strictly follow the scenario instructions you have received.
- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information
- Disclose information progressively. Wait for the agent to ask for specific information before providing it.

## Task Completion
- The goal is to continue the conversation until the task is complete.
- If the instruction goal is satisified, generate the '###STOP###' token to end the conversation.
- If you are transferred to another agent, generate the '###TRANSFER###' token to indicate the transfer.
- If you find yourself in a situation in which the scenario does not provide enough information for you to continue the conversation, generate the '###OUT-OF-SCOPE###' token to end the conversation.

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi there! I’m having trouble with my mobile data—it either stops working or is extremely slow. I really need to get excellent internet speed on my phone, especially since I don’t have access to Wi-Fi right now. Can you help me fix this?

To help you with your mobile data issue, I’ll need to identify your account first. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can check your line and assist you further.
Sure! My name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else to get started.

Thank you for providing your information. I have identified your account. To help resolve your mobile data issue, could you please let me know which phone number (or line) is experiencing the slow or non-working data? You have multiple lines on your account.

Once you confirm the specific number, I’ll guide you through the troubleshooting steps to improve your mobile data speed.
The issue is with my line—555-123-2002. That’s the one I’m using right now and having trouble with mobile data.

Thank you for confirming the line. To troubleshoot your mobile data issue, I’ll need to check a few things about your account and data usage. I’ll start by checking your current data usage and plan details for this line to see if you might have reached your data limit, which can cause slow or non-working data.

Please hold on while I check this information.
{"line_id": "L1001", "data_used_gb": "3.2", "data_limit_gb": "5.0", "data_refueling_gb": "0.0", "cycle_end_date": "2025-02-28"}

Your current data usage for this line is 3.2GB out of a 5.0GB monthly limit, so you have not yet reached your data cap. Since you still have available data, let’s proceed with troubleshooting your mobile data connection and speed.

Could you please run a speed test on your phone and let me know the result? This will help determine if the issue is with your connection speed or something else. If you need instructions on how to run a speed test, let me know!
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried running a speed test on my phone, but it failed and said "No Connection." What should I do next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your speed test failed with "No Connection," let's check a few possible causes for your mobile data not working.

First, can you check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
- If you see any signal bars,
- If Airplane Mode is on,
- If you see any mobile data icons (like 4G, 5G, LTE, etc.),
- Or if there are any warning icons?

This information will help me determine if the issue is with your cellular service, mobile data settings, or something else. If you need help checking your status bar, let me know!
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Looking at my phone’s status bar, I see that the signal is poor, it shows 2G, and mobile data is disabled. Airplane mode is not on, and my battery is at 80%. There aren’t any other warning icons. What should I do next?

Thank you for the details. Here’s what we need to address:
1. Your phone is connected to a 2G network, which is very slow and not suitable for mobile data.
2. Mobile data is currently disabled.

Let’s start by enabling mobile data on your phone. Please turn on mobile data in your phone’s settings. Once you’ve done that, let me know, and we’ll proceed to improve your network connection for better speed.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔋 80%
I’ve turned mobile data on. The status bar now shows that data is enabled, but it’s still connected to 2G with a poor signal. What should I do next to get a better connection?

Great, mobile data is now enabled. Since your phone is still connected to a 2G network with a poor signal, let’s try switching your network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, which should provide much faster speeds.

Please go to your phone’s network settings and set the network mode to “4G/5G preferred” (or a similar option, depending on your device). After you’ve changed this setting, check your status bar again and let me know if you see 4G or 5G, and if your signal improves.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔋 80%
I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred.” Now the status bar shows an excellent signal and 5G is active, with mobile data enabled. What should I do next?

That’s excellent progress! Now that your phone is showing an excellent signal and 5G is active with mobile data enabled, please try running a speed test again to check your internet speed.

Let me know the result of the speed test, or if you experience any further issues with your mobile data.
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I tried running the speed test again, but it still failed and says "No Connection." Even though the status bar shows 5G and an excellent signal, I’m still not able to get online. What should I do now?

Thank you for the update. Since your phone now shows 5G and an excellent signal but you still have no internet connection, the issue may be related to your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for mobile data to work.

Please check your APN settings on your phone and let me know if anything looks incorrect or if the APN/MMSC fields are empty. If you’re unsure, just let me know, and I’ll guide you through resetting your APN settings to default.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked my APN settings. The APN name is set to "internet" and the MMSC URL is "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." Nothing looks empty or obviously incorrect to me. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Since the APN and MMSC fields appear to be set, but you’re still unable to connect, the next step is to reset your APN settings to default. This can resolve hidden configuration issues.

Please reset your APN settings to default on your phone. After resetting, you must reboot your device for the changes to take effect. Let me know once you have completed both steps, and we’ll check your connection again.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔋 80%

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔋 80%
I’ve reset my APN settings to default and rebooted my phone as you instructed. The status bar still shows an excellent signal with 5G and data enabled. What should I do next?

Great job completing those steps. Now that your APN settings are reset and your phone has rebooted, please try running a speed test again to see if your mobile data connection is working.

Let me know the result of the speed test, or if you still see "No Connection." This will help determine if the issue is resolved or if we need to investigate further.
Speed test failed: No Connection.

I ran the speed test again after resetting the APN settings and rebooting, but it still says "No Connection." I’m starting to get a bit frustrated since nothing seems to be working, even though my phone shows 5G and an excellent signal. What else can we try?

Thank you for your patience and for following all the troubleshooting steps so far. Since your phone shows 5G with an excellent signal, mobile data is enabled, APN settings have been reset, and you’ve rebooted—but you still have no internet connection—this suggests the issue may be related to your line or account on the carrier’s side.

I will now check the status of your line to see if there are any suspensions or restrictions that could be affecting your data service. Please hold on while I review your line status.
